steps.title: Start from roles, not from your degree title
steps.detail: Find five people doing work you would like to do in three to five years. Note their job titles, employers and the skills listed in their profiles. That list, not your syllabus, is the target you are building towards.

steps.title: Close the skills gap in public
steps.detail: Pick the two skills that appear most often and build something that proves them: a portfolio project, a published analysis, a volunteer client, a small app. Evidence beats a certificate you cannot demonstrate.

steps.title: Get one foot inside the industry
steps.detail: An internship, part-time role, research assistantship or freelance brief gives you vocabulary, references and a sense of how the work is actually done. Apply early, including to smaller organisations that reply faster.

steps.title: Ask for conversations, not for jobs
steps.detail: Request fifteen minutes to ask how someone entered the field, what they wish they had learned earlier and who else you should speak to. Most people answer a specific, short request and ignore a generic request for opportunities.

steps.title: Apply in a deliberate pattern
steps.detail: Ten tailored applications with a revised CV and cover letter beat a hundred generic ones. Keep a tracker with the role, contact, date and outcome so you can see which version of your application is working.

steps.title: Keep the first year deliberate
steps.detail: In the first 90 days, learn how decisions are made, deliver one visible piece of work well and find a mentor. Ask for a development plan at your review rather than waiting to be offered one.

playbooks.first_roles: Graduate engineer, junior developer, data analyst, site or process engineer, QA engineer
playbooks.credentials: Professional registration (ECSA in South Africa, COREN in Nigeria, ICE or IMechE in the UK), cloud or vendor certifications only where the job advert asks for them
playbooks.proof: Two or three projects with a working result, a GitHub or portfolio page, and a short write-up of a problem you solved
playbooks.bodies: Engineering councils and institutions in your country, IEEE, ACM, local developer communities

playbooks.first_roles: Intern or community-service practitioner, research assistant, clinical trial coordinator, laboratory technologist, public health officer
playbooks.credentials: Registration with your health professions council (HPCSA, MDCN and equivalents), specialization exams, good clinical practice certification
playbooks.proof: Clinical rotations, audit or quality-improvement projects, a conference abstract, volunteer health outreach
playbooks.bodies: Your health professions council, professional societies, WHO and ministry of health bulletins

playbooks.first_roles: Graduate analyst, audit trainee, operations associate, investment analyst, supply chain planner
playbooks.credentials: ACA, ACCA, CIMA or CFA for finance; a recognised graduate scheme for general management
playbooks.proof: A financial model, a case competition, a dashboard built in Excel or Power BI, an internship in a finance function
playbooks.bodies: Professional accountancy bodies, CFA Institute, industry associations and chamber of commerce events

playbooks.first_roles: Candidate attorney or trainee, legal researcher, compliance analyst, paralegal, policy officer
playbooks.credentials: Admission to your jurisdiction's bar or law society, LLM only where it serves a specific practice area
playbooks.proof: Moot court, legal aid clinic work, a clerkship, published case notes, contract drafting samples
playbooks.bodies: Law society or bar association, law reform commissions, human rights organisations

playbooks.first_roles: Policy or research assistant, monitoring and evaluation officer, programme officer, data collector, community engagement coordinator
playbooks.credentials: Short courses in statistics, monitoring and evaluation, or research methods; a master's for policy roles
playbooks.proof: A research report you wrote, survey design or analysis work, an internship with an NGO or think tank
playbooks.bodies: Think tanks, NGO networks, evaluation associations, university research centres

playbooks.first_roles: Teaching assistant, tutor, curriculum or content developer, education technology associate, school administrator
playbooks.credentials: Teaching qualification or PGCE where required, subject-specific certification, safeguarding training
playbooks.proof: Classroom hours, learner outcomes you can describe, a resource or lesson series you built
playbooks.bodies: Teaching councils, subject associations, teacher networks and school clusters

playbooks.first_roles: Editorial assistant, content producer, communications officer, researcher, freelance writer or designer
playbooks.credentials: A portfolio matters more than a certificate; add short courses in editing, data journalism or design tools
playbooks.proof: Three published or self-published pieces, a portfolio site, client or student publication work
playbooks.bodies: Writers' guilds, press clubs, arts councils, publishing and media associations

playbooks.first_roles: Extension officer, environmental officer, GIS technician, sustainability analyst, field research assistant
playbooks.credentials: GIS and remote sensing training, environmental impact assessment registration where regulated
playbooks.proof: Field or laboratory work, a mapping project, an internship with a conservation or agricultural organisation
playbooks.bodies: Agricultural and environmental professional bodies, CGIAR centres, conservation NGOs

networking: Write a one-line introduction: what you study, what you can do and what you are looking for next.
Keep a simple tracker of everyone you speak to, what you learned and when to follow up.
Follow up once after a week with something useful, not simply a reminder that you exist.
Attend one event a month in your field and speak to three people rather than collecting contacts.
Ask former lecturers and alumni first; they already have a reason to answer you.
